newsitem.title: USA: Walgreen delays on-line pharmacy plans.
newsitem.headline: Walgreen delays on-line pharmacy plans.

text.p: Walgreen Co said Wednesday it is temporarily suspending the rollout of its new computer-based, dial-in prescription program because of system problems that cropped up as more pharmacies came on-line.
Walgreen president and chief operating officer L. Daniel Jorndt said the company's Intercom Plus rollout "will be halted until problems we encountered as more stores signed on are fixed."

Jorndt said 800 Walgreen pharmacies are currently using Intercom Plus. He did not say when installation at more pharmacies will resume, although he said he would be "very disappointed if we didn't have all of our stores on the system by Christmas of 1997."

Walgreen spent $100 million over the last four years developing Intercom Plus, which is designed to help Walgreen pharmacies better manage workflow and increase productivity and volume. It allows patients to enter prescription refill information with touch-tone telephones and alerts pharmacists of the best time to prepare the prescription, he added.
The system can even tell pharmacists the optimum bottle size to use when dispensing pills, Jorndt said.
"The idea," Jorndt said, "is to reduce the amount of time a patient spends waiting to pick up a prescription at our stores.
However, the rollout has not been as smooth as the company hoped, he said. "We were having system problems, computer crashes, that sort of thing," Jorndt explained.
Walgreen hopes between 70 percent and 80 percent of its prescription orders will use the Intercom Plus system by the time its marketing campaign begins in late 1997 or early 1998.
Walgreen operated 2,238 drugstores in 34 states and Puerto Rico as of December 31, and said this week it will open 230 stores in 1997. The company said it opened 210 units in 1996.
"We're on track to have 3,000 stores open by the year 2000," Jorndt said, adding that plans call for 2,400 of those stores to be freestanding units.
Walgreen officials also reiterated that the company will expand by building new stores, not through acquisitions.
"Walgreens does not intend to acquire anyone," Charles Walgreen III, the company's chairman and chief executive officer, said. "We don't want anyone else's rejects."

Earlier this week, Walgreen reported net income of $75 million for the first quarter, which ended November 30, up from $63.7 million a year ago, and sales of $3.0 billion, versus $2.7 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 1996.
Company officials also said comparable store sales for the holiday season were up 7.7 percent, well above its targets.
"It was an excellent Christmas," Jorndt said.
Walgreen shares closed down 7/8 Wednesday at 39-1/8.
